newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bayernverein says wants to stay independent.
newsitem.headline: Bayernverein says wants to stay independent.

text.p: Bayerische Vereinsbank AG, which has been at the heart of takeover speculation after rival Deutsche Bank AG said it had amassed a 5.2 percent stake in the bank, said on Friday it aimed to stay independent.
"We want to remain an independent, Munich-based bank," chief executive Albrecht Schmidt told a news conference here.
Schmidt also said he did not know whether Deutsche had bought additional shares in his bank since it disclosed its stake in July.
"I do not know if it is buying additional shares but if it is, I know other investors are buying our shares as well," Schmidt said in response to a question.
Bayernverein shares have risen sharply since Deutsche's disclosure and a banking source said earlier this month that the Frankfurt-based giant appeared to be buying additional shares.
"The shares of Bayerische Vereinsbank are esteemed by many investors," Schmidt said. "I can only congratulate them."

Asked how long Bayernverein expected to remain independent, Schmidt said: "So long as we remain profitable and continue to have a sharp profile, and as long as shareholders and customers continue to believe it would be a bad thing not to have Bayerische Vereinsbank."
Deutsche has said that it took a stake in Beyernverein in order to deter potential bidders, but that it had no immediate plans to increase the stake.
